title: Who can see your work?
hook: Would a fast colleague have the same effect if they could not observe you?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate proximity to a productive peer from being visible to that peer.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate proximity to a productive peer from being visible to that peer.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In toy case A, the productive peer can see you but you cannot see the peer. Which visibility indicator is one? Toy inputs A=[1, 0, 5]; B=[0, 1, 5].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[1, 0, 5], [0, 1, 5]]. Labels: Visible to peer, Peer visible, Distance.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Being close to a productive peer and being visible to that peer are different features. The two toy arrangements keep distance fixed and reverse visibility. That exposes the design distinction rather than assigning a productivity effect.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Peer sees you=0, You see peer=1, Distance m=5. What is Visible to peer? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

claims.text: In the toy diagram, Me and Peer name the two actors. The sees arrow runs from the viewer to the person seen. Distance stays at 5 m in both cases.
claims.source: The two graph cases in spec.ts; short node names replace long indicator labels, with the same model inputs and output ledger.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Peer sees you=0, You see peer=1, Distance m=5. What is Visible to peer?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Supermarket cashiers worked faster when a highly productive colleague could see them (Mas & Moretti, 2009).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate proximity to a productive peer from being visible to that peer.
